summary: Take V_w = F ∗ X_w with X_w the right derivatives (along the word w) of a smooth smear of ψ_λ; the derivatives stay in the discrete series module with norms controlled by the filtration, and the Schur bound is the bound for convolutions of F by elements of D_λ (Schur orthogonality). (Lines 29–31 are the end of the statement; the line census takes the `:=` of the statement's `let e := …` for the start of the value, so they stand in intro_lines.)

steps.lean:
intro e fx H; obtain ⟨⟨β, hβ⟩, ⟨o, u, -⟩, k⟩ := exists_smear_dsCoeffSmooth_eq hg l.dsGenerator,
    hg.isUnitaryCasimirGe_dsAction, isIdempotentKernel_psiInFrame hg
steps.claim: Introduce e, fx: F ∗ e = F, and H: the bound on B; obtain β (smooth, compactly supported) whose smear of ψ_λ is the generator of D_λ (hβ), the Casimir facts (o, u), and k: e is an idempotent kernel.

steps.lean:
let π := frameEquiv (ε := ε); let γ w := (bumpDeriv.adTwist p.p⁻¹).word w β
  let S := smear l.dsCoeffSmooth.1; let X w g := l.formalDegree * S (γ w) (π g)
steps.claim: π = frameEquiv; γ_w = the word w applied to β by the twisted derivative action (adTwist by p⁻¹); S = the smear of ψ_λ; X_w(g) = deg_λ·S(γ_w)(π(g)).
c: F is continuous (F = F ∗ e, a convolution with the integrable kernel e).

steps.lean:
have hb : IsBoundedMeasurable e :=
    .of ⟨_, fun _ ↦ by grw [norm_mul, HCParam.psiInFrame, norm_dsCoeff_le_one hg]⟩ k.1
steps.claim: hb: e is bounded and measurable (|ψ_λ| ≤ 1).

steps.lean:
have t w : Integrable (X w) ∧ convolve e (X w) = X w ∧ convolve F (X w) = smear _ c (γ w) ∘ π :=
    have z := measurePreserving_frameEquiv.integrable_comp_of_integrable (γ w).2.integrable; by
    rw [← show convolve e (_ ∘ π) = X w by
      ext; simp [X, S, e, π, convolve, ↓← integral_comp_frameEquiv, ← map_mul,
        mul_left_comm _ (l.formalDegree : ℂ)]; tauto, ← hb.convolve_assoc k.2 z, show convolve e e =
      e by ext; simpa [k.4] using! k.integral_inv_mul_translate _ 1, ← hW.convolve_assoc k.2 z, fx]
    use integrable_convolve k.2 z, rfl, by ext; simp [π, convolve, ← integral_comp_frameEquiv]
steps.claim: t: for every word w, X_w is integrable, e ∗ X_w = X_w, and F ∗ X_w = smear(c)(γ_w) ∘ π.
steps.typed_fact: Integrable (X w) ∧ convolve e (X w) = X w ∧ convolve F (X w) = smear _ c (γ w) ∘ π

steps.lean:
show convolve e (_ ∘ π) = X w by
      ext; simp [X, S, e, π, convolve, ↓← integral_comp_frameEquiv, ← map_mul,
        mul_left_comm _ (l.formalDegree : ℂ)]; tauto, ← hb.convolve_assoc k.2 z,
steps.claim: e ∗ (γ_w ∘ π) = X_w = deg_λ·S(γ_w) ∘ π: convolving the twisted derivative γ_w of the compact smooth bump, moved by π, with e gives deg_λ times its smear (unfold; integrals transported by π); then associativity of convolutions.

steps.lean:
show convolve e e =
      e by ext; simpa [k.4] using! k.integral_inv_mul_translate _ 1, ← hW.convolve_assoc k.2 z, fx]
    use integrable_convolve k.2 z, rfl, by ext; simp [π, convolve, ← integral_comp_frameEquiv]
steps.claim: e ∗ e = e (k); associativity for F and fx give the identities; X_w is integrable (a convolution).

steps.lean: use fun w ↦ ⟨_, hW.continuous_convolve (t w).1⟩, by simp [X]; erw [hβ, fx], fun w ↦ ?_
steps.claim: Take V_w = F ∗ X_w (continuous); V_[] = F by hβ and fx; it remains, for each w, the Bessel, derivative and Schur parts.

steps.lean: let ⟨j, ex, a⟩ := t w; dsimp
steps.claim: Unpack t at w: j (X_w integrable), ex (e ∗ X_w = X_w), a (F ∗ X_w = smear(c)(γ_w) ∘ π).

steps.lean:
obtain ⟨x, -, b, s⟩ : ∃ x ∈ l.dsAction.filtration ε l.dsGenerator w.length,
      ‖x‖ ≤ ((𝔰.r + 1) ^ 4 * (L + 𝔰.r + 1 + w.length)) ^ w.length ∧ S (γ w) = x.1
  · refine w.rec ⟨_, GlModule.self_mem_filtration, u.le, hβ⟩ fun q w ⟨x, m, b, s⟩ ↦ ⟨_,
      ((isKHighest_dsGenerator hg).norm_apply_le_of_mem_filtration o (abs_lowestKType_le hg hL) m
      _).imp_right (⟨·.trans ?_, rightDeriv_smear _ _ s _⟩)⟩
    simp [inv_eq_left_inv p.2.1, p.2, l2_opNorm_single, pow_succ' _ w.length]
    grw [b]; gcongr <;> simp
steps.claim: There is x in the |w|-th filtration of the discrete series module with ‖x‖ ≤ ((r+1)⁴(L + r + 1 + |w|))^{|w|} and S(γ_w) = x: induction on w, each letter a right derivative (rightDeriv_smear) bounded on K-highest vectors of the filtration (lowest K-type at most L + r + 1 + |w|) times the norm of a matrix unit conjugated by p.
steps.typed_fact:
∃ x ∈ l.dsAction.filtration ε l.dsGenerator w.length,
      ‖x‖ ≤ ((𝔰.r + 1) ^ 4 * (L + 𝔰.r + 1 + w.length)) ^ w.length ∧ S (γ w) = x.1

steps.lean:
use ?_, fun g Z r h ↦ a ▸ .congr_deriv (hasDerivAt_smear _ _ c ?_) (by
    erw [(bumpDeriv.adTwist p.p⁻¹).apply_eq_sum Z]; simp [t, -smear_apply]; rfl), fun hw φ i ↦ ?_
steps.claim: Remaining: V_w is Bessel; the derivative law (V_w ∘ γ)' = Σ_{a,b} X_{ab}·V_{(a,b)w}(γ) along every real curve with γ' = γX (derivative of the smear, the twisted action expanded in matrix units); and the Schur bound.

steps.lean:
constructor <;> simp +contextual [hW.convolve_right j, convolve, mul_assoc, hW.2, hW.3, smul_comm
    (X w _), integral_smul, ← ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm, hW.integrable_smul j.comp_inv]
steps.claim: The Bessel laws pass to F ∗ X_w (the convolution acts on the right).
The derivative side condition (the curve conjugated by p).

steps.lean:
show _ ^ 2 = (∫ g, ‖X w g‖ ^ 2) / l.formalDegree by
    simpa [X, s, π, field, Complex.mul_conj', ← Complex.ofReal_pow, integral_complex_ofReal,
    mul_pow, ← integral_comp_frameEquiv] using! congr($(hg.toL2_spec.2.2 x x 1).re),
    ← hW.lintegral_sq_convolve_convolve_le rfl ?_ hW.2 h2 j k ?_ fx hb ex i] <;> simp [convolve,
    HCParam.psiInFrame]
steps.claim: ‖x‖² = ∫|X_w|²/deg_λ (Schur orthogonality for D_λ), and the convolution bound for Bessel functions (lintegral_sq_convolve_convolve_le) gives ∫|∫ φ(y)(F ∗ X_w)(γy) dy|² ≤ (∫|X_w|²/deg_λ)·deg_λ⁻¹∫|F|²·∫|φ|².
